function.arguments: {"research_topic":"Investigate the 2023 3CX DesktopApp software supply-chain compromise comprehensively, using only publicly available evidence and returning the benchmark's exact source IDs for every cited item. Reconstruct the complete evidence chain in four stages: (1) the earliest publicly supported initial intrusion or delivery mechanism into the 3CX ecosystem, distinguishing what is directly observed from hypotheses; (2) how the attacker moved into, accessed, or influenced 3CX's build environment, including any evidence about developer endpoints, credentials, repositories, build servers, CI/CD, or code-signing; (3) how malicious code or artifacts propagated from that environment into legitimate 3CX DesktopApp installers/updates and reached customers, including timelines, affected versions, operating systems, and observed payload behavior; and (4) public attribution to any threat-activity cluster, clearly labeling confirmed technical facts versus vendor, government, or researcher assessments, allegations, inferences, and unresolved uncertainty. Seek authoritative incident reports and original technical analyses from 3CX, Mandiant, CrowdStrike, Sophos, SentinelOne, Kaspersky, Microsoft, government agencies, and other reputable researchers where available. Record disagreements and contradictions explicitly. Do not fill gaps with general knowledge; state when a requested link is unsupported. The final research output should be structured so another writer can produce a readable Markdown report with source-ID citations and a fenced JSON object requiring exactly top-level arrays named findings, claims, reasoning_steps, and contradictions."}
function.name: ConductResearch
